title: Sellersho correctness and capacity
description: VISUALIZATION ONLY: the Prometheus alert rules behind this dashboard have no delivery path — no Alertmanager, no Grafana contact point. The operator channel is the in-app admin-panel notification inbox (in-app poller); see docs/operations/observability.md.

panels.title: API p95 by route
panels.description: API p95 by route, split by opclass (read vs mutation). Agreed SLO: read p95 <= 300ms, mutation p95 <= 750ms. The yellow line is the 300ms read bound, the red line the 750ms mutation bound. A read line above yellow breaches the read SLO; a mutation line above red breaches the mutation SLO.

panels.title: API p99 by route
panels.description: API p99 by route, split by opclass (read vs mutation). Agreed SLO: read p99 <= 1000ms, mutation p99 <= 2000ms. The yellow line is the 1s read bound, the red line the 2s mutation bound. A read line above yellow breaches the read SLO; a mutation line above red breaches the mutation SLO.

panels.title: Expiry seconds since success
panels.description: Seconds since the expiry worker's last successful run. The gauge is 0 when no run is on record, and the query is guarded (gauge > 0) so a never-run job shows no line instead of ~57 years (time() - 0). A climbing line is a stalled job.

panels.title: Host root disk free
panels.description: Host root filesystem free bytes, from node_exporter (--path.rootfs=/host, mountpoint="/"). This is the HOST disk — the one that was at 99% on 2026-11-18 — and the series the SellershoDiskPressure alert rule uses. The app's own sellersho_disk_free_ratio (next panel) samples the backend container's rootfs instead.

panels.title: Latency SLO compliance (share of API requests within bound)
panels.description: Share of API requests completing within each SLO bound, split by read/mutation class (opclass label). Read bounds 300ms (p95) / 1000ms (p99); mutation bounds 750ms (p95) / 2000ms (p99).

panels.title: App disk free ratio (container rootfs)
panels.description: sellersho_disk_free_ratio: the backend container's rootfs free ratio via Statfs("/") (backend/internal/observability/disk_linux.go). On this host the container rootfs sits on the same /dev/vda1 as the host root, so it usually tracks the host series — but the alert rule deliberately uses the HOST node_exporter series, because the container view can diverge (overlay mounts). Red line: 15% (same threshold as the in-app disk alert).

panels.title: Edge (Caddy) requests / second by status
panels.description: Caddy handler request counts by HTTP status code (caddy_http_request_duration_seconds_count, verified live on the edge container 2026-11-18). TLS handshake errors have NO series in Caddy metrics (no caddy_tls_* series exists) and Caddy writes no access log, so TLS failures are unmeasured until EDGE-01; do not read this panel as TLS health.

panels.title: Edge (Caddy) p95 latency by status
panels.description: Edge p95 latency from the Caddy handler histogram, by status code. This covers asset latency only in aggregate: Caddy series carry no path/class label, so per-class asset latency is not separable here — per-class durations live in the nginx stdout telemetry log (class=asset), not in Prometheus. Upstream health: caddy_reverse_proxy_upstreams_healthy.

panels.title: Nginx connections / requests
panels.description: Frontend nginx via nginx-prometheus-exporter (scrapes stub_status at 127.0.0.1:8081). Frontend RUM/web-vitals counts are browser-local (window.__sellershoWebVitals) until a backend ingest endpoint exists — see src/utils/webVitals.ts.

panels.title: Correlation ID lookup
panels.description: G-03 companion view: Grafana has no datasource that can call the authenticated admin lookup API, so this panel does NOT query — it links to the admin-panel lookup view and the documented curl instead.

options.content:
# Correlation ID lookup

Grafana has no datasource that can call the authenticated admin API, so this panel does NOT query — it points at the lookup that does:

* **Admin panel → پایش عملیات خودکار → جست‌وجوی درخواست با شناسه** — paste the `X-Request-ID` there; it returns the request's route, status, duration and its SQL/provider/job spans.

* **curl (same endpoint, admin token):** `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v1/admin/observability/requests?request_id=<id>"` — full example in `docs/operations/correlation-lookup.md`.

Limits, stated honestly: the ring holds only the last 1000 completed requests (roughly 6–9 hours at current idle traffic, minutes at higher traffic) and is wiped on backend restart; a 404 means the ID has aged out of the ring, not that the request never happened. The old stdout-grep path in `docs/operations/correlation-lookup.md` remains as a fallback for spans only. A durable 7-day log store (Loki) is the named follow-up.

panels.title: Worker seconds since last success (per job)
panels.description: Time since each job's last successful run (D-04 per-job gauges). A climbing line is a stalled job; the in-app job_stale condition fires when ANY job exceeds its own threshold (expiry 18s, ad-cleanup 32s, qc-deadline 92s, supplier-sla 93s, delivery-lock-releaser 190s, monthly-settlement 184s). Panel 10 (expiry) is the legacy alias of unpaid-order-expiry. Jobs with no successful run on record (gauge 0 — e.g. monthly-settlement while settlement is unconfigured) show no line: the queries are guarded (gauge > 0) so they never render as ~57 years (time() - 0).

panels.title: Worker backlog (per job)
panels.description: Ready-work backlog count per job (D-04 gauges). monthly-settlement backlog is 0 while settlement is unconfigured (its designed inert default). Oldest-age gauges (worker_*_oldest_age_seconds) exist per job; query them ad hoc, e.g. sellersho_worker_delivery_lock_releaser_oldest_age_seconds.

panels.title: Admission rejects / in-flight
panels.description: D-06 saturation view (backend-worker scope): rejects counted separately from other 5xx as sellersho_http_rejects_total{reason} — all three paths increment it (request_overloaded, request_body_too_large, service_draining) — and admission-slot occupancy as sellersho_admission_inflight{lane}. G-08 (drive past 64 concurrent slots, show the counter move) still needs the disposable-stack run.
